changelog:
• Backup: the hosted Cloud Backup is replaced by backing up to a folder of your choice — Google Drive, Nextcloud, an SD card or the phone itself, anything the system folder picker offers. Files are encrypted on the phone before they are written, under the same recovery code bookmark sync uses; the Backups list, restore, open-without-restoring, "Free up space" and the download menu's "Back up" all work against the folder. Nothing goes through a Firedown server. Choosing the folder asks where: cloud storage (with a picture of the picker's ☰ button, where Android keeps your cloud apps), the SD card when one is in, or somewhere else. Firedown then checks that it can actually save files in the folder you pick before using it, and warns if you pick the phone's own Download/Firedown folder. A backup that fails says why, in the Backups list and as a notification
• Backup: the Backup screen states where the backup is ("Google Drive › Backups") on a Backup folder row, which is also where you change it, with a warning that the old folder keeps its files; the standalone "Change folder" button is gone. A download being backed up shows it on its own row in Downloads ("Backing up… · 32%"), and Cancel is on that row's menu and on the notification, which now shows progress
• Backup: a third kind of place, "WebDAV server" — Nextcloud, ownCloud, a home NAS or any WebDAV address, signed in to inside Firedown with no other app. Type the server name (Nextcloud's WebDAV address is found for you), a user and an app password; Firedown checks it can write there before using it, asks before trusting a server that made its own certificate (showing the fingerprint to compare), and backs up over the network only when there is one. If the server stops answering, the Backup screen says so and "Reconnect" opens the sign-in again with the saved details. The "can't reach your backup folder" notification now names the folder instead of the file that was being backed up
• Removed with the hosted service: storage credit and its Bitcoin payments, "Pair a browser" and the web client. Restore anything you still want from the old Cloud Backup to this phone BEFORE updating, then back it up into a folder
• Backup: "I have a recovery code" now says what it does under the folder model — the code is the key, and a second phone reads the first one's backups only once it also uses the same backup folder; the row, the dialog, the replace warning, the QR hint and the confirmation no longer claim that the code alone shares a backup
• Send directly: the transfer no longer needs the screen — it runs in the background with a progress notification (Cancel from there, tap to come back), and a shared link stays valid for 15 minutes without the sender babysitting it. On the same Wi-Fi the sender now sees a list of phones that have "Receive a file" open and taps one; the receiver gets the request with Accept/Decline. The link and the QR remain for a phone that is not on this network ("Anywhere")
• Send directly: a transfer that stops moving or loses its connection now ends with a message that says so (re-share the same file to continue where it left off) instead of sitting at the same percent; a slow transfer no longer fails at 100 % while waiting for the receiver's confirmation; the relay credential is refreshed before a share instead of being reused with minutes of life left, which is what made relayed transfers die mid-way; a share without internet skips the relay at once and says so if no path is found; Wi-Fi is kept awake and the engine kept alive while a transfer runs in the background
• Captured videos keep the names a page declares for them when they play inside an embedded frame; every clip in firedown.app's own demo was captured as "Firedown · demo"
